Redis is an in-memory data structure store that can be used as a database, cache, and message broker. It supports data structures such as strings, hashes, lists, and sets.
Vector databases store embeddings and allow similarity search. Redis Stack includes vector search capabilities through the RediSearch module, making it useful for RAG pipelines.
Machine learning models convert text into embeddings — dense numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning. Cosine similarity is commonly used to compare these vectors.
RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It combines information retrieval with large language models to produce grounded, factual answers from a knowledge base.
Agentic RAG extends basic RAG by giving an LLM the ability to call tools, refine its search, and reason over multiple retrieval steps before generating a final answer.
Google Gemini is a multimodal large language model developed by Google DeepMind. It is accessible via Google AI Studio and supports tool use, function calling, and long context.
Google ADK (Agent Development Kit) is a Python framework for building LLM-powered agents. It provides abstractions for tools, memory, sessions, and multi-agent orchestration.
Traditional keyword search uses BM25 or TF-IDF scoring and fails on semantic queries. For example, searching 'automobile' will not match documents that only mention 'car'.
HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is an approximate nearest neighbour algorithm used in vector databases. It offers sub-linear query time with high recall.
Redis can be used purely as a caching layer to speed up web applications by storing frequently accessed data in RAM, reducing load on the primary database.
Redis as a vector store is different from Redis as a cache. As a vector store it stores high-dimensional embeddings; as a cache it stores key-value pairs with TTL expiry.
Semantic search finds documents based on meaning rather than exact word matches. A query about 'automobile' can match documents about 'car', 'vehicle', or 'sedan'.
Sentence Transformers is a Python library that fine-tunes BERT-based models to produce semantically meaningful sentence embeddings, commonly used in semantic search and RAG.
The cosine distance between two vectors is 1 minus their cosine similarity. A distance of 0 means identical direction; a distance of 1 means orthogonal (unrelated) vectors.
Hallucination in LLMs refers to confident generation of factually incorrect information. RAG reduces hallucination by grounding responses in retrieved, factual documents.
An AI agent is an autonomous system that perceives its environment, reasons about it, and takes actions. In Agentic RAG the agent decides what to search and when to stop searching.
Function calling in Gemini allows developers to define Python functions as tools. The model decides when to call them and passes structured arguments, enabling agentic behaviour.
When comparing Redis as a vector database versus dedicated vector databases like Pinecone or Weaviate, Redis excels in low-latency caching but may lack advanced indexing features.
